products.name: Screen Awesome
products.tagline: The free screen recorder that cannot upload your video
products.description: Every screen recorder promises not to misuse your recordings. Screen Awesome can't: it requests zero host permissions, so Chrome itself blocks it from reaching any server. Check it in chrome://extensions before you install. Record a tab, screen or camera to MP4. Auto-zoom glides a virtual camera to every click. Screenshot a region or a full scrolling page. Annotate with arrows, blur, redaction, step counters and text — all editable vectors. Free, unlocked, no account, no watermark.

source_pages.title: Screen Awesome — Free Screen Recorder That Can't Upload
source_pages.excerpt: Screen Awesome — Free Screen Recorder That Can't Upload rich result for the product itself FAQPage -> the FAQ can surface directly in search Person -> establishes authorship, which E-E-A-T leans on Every FAQ answer below is a copy of the visible text further down the page. Google requires them to match; if you edit one, edit both. --> Skip to content Screen Awesome Features Privacy FAQ Add to Chrome Zero host permissions The screen recorder that cannot upload your recordings. Every other capture tool asks you to trust its privacy policy. Screen Awesome asks you to check its permissions instead — there are none for any website, so there is no server it is allowed to reach. Record, screenshot and annotate, entirely on your own machine. Add to Chrome — free How to verify it Free and unlocked. No account, no watermark, no trial. Host permissions None Account required No Recording format MP4 Paid features Zero Everything unlocked, nothing upsold The tools other extensions charge for are the reason anyone annotates a screenshot. They are all here, and they all stay here. Local-only by construction Captures are written to your browser's own storage the moment they exist. No account, no sync, no analytics, and no host permissions — so there is nothing to opt out of. Auto-zoom to your clicks Recording a tab notes where you click, then the studio glides a virtual camera onto each one and pans between them. Screencast polish without an editor. Annotate anything Arrows, pen, highlighter, shapes, text in any system font, speech bubbles, step counters, emoji stamps, crop and image insert. Every mark stays editable. MP4, not just WebM Records to MP4 wherever Chrome can, so your file drops straight into Slack, Docs or a video editor. Export as MP4, WebM or an animated GIF. Screenshots, the hard cases too Visible area, a dragged region, or a full page stitched together as it scrolls. Capture outside the browser, or on a timer to catch a menu that won't stay open. Voice, camera and control Mix in your microphone and the tab's own audio, composite a webcam bubble you can move mid-recording, pause and resume, cap the length, and draw on the page live. Privacy you can check, not privacy you're promised "We respect your privacy" is a sentence anyone can write. This is a limitation Chrome enforces on the extension, and you can confirm it before you install. What the permission list means in practice Capability Screen Awesome Typical capture extension Can read the pages you browse No — no host permissions Often, via broad site access Can upload your captures No — architecturally impossible Yes, that is the cloud feature Account or sign-in Never Usually required to share Analytics or telemetry None Common Paywalled annotation tools None Arrow, blur, counter, bubble How to verify it yourself Open chrome://extensions in a new tab. Find Screen Awesome and click Details . Look at Site access . It reads none — the extension is not permitted to contact any website, which is what makes uploading impossible rather than merely disallowed. The extension's own settings page has a Check its permissions button that opens this screen for you. Frequently asked questions Short answers. If yours isn't here, email nitinbhaiviras@gmail.com . Is Screen Awesome really free? Yes, and there is no paid tier to upgrade to. Every annotation tool is unlocked, including the arrow, blur, redaction, step counter, speech bubble and image insertion that comparable extensions put behind a subscription. There are no watermarks, no recording length limits imposed by us, and no account to create. Where are my recordings stored? In your own browser, using IndexedDB, on the machine you recorded them on. They are written there the instant they exist. Nothing is copied to a server, because the extension requests no host permissions and therefore has no server it is allowed to contact. How can I verify that nothing is uploaded? Open chrome://extensions , find Screen Awesome and look at its Site access line: it has none. An extension with no host permissions cannot make a request to any website, so this is a limit Chrome enforces rather than a promise we are asking you to trust. You can also open the extension's settings page and press Check its permissions to go straight there. Does it record in MP4 or WebM? MP4 wherever Chrome supports encoding it, falling back to WebM otherwise. MP4 matters because it drops straight into Slack, Google Docs, Premiere and almost every video editor with no conversion step. The studio can also convert on export, and can render a clip as an animated GIF. What is auto-zoom to clicks? While you record a tab, Screen Awesome notes where you click. Afterwards the studio replays the recording through a virtual camera that glides in on each click and pans between them, which is the polish that normally means editing a screencast by hand. You can preview it live, switch it off, or bake it into the exported file. Can it record my whole screen and other applications? Yes. Choose Screen in the recorder and Chrome will ask which screen, window or application to share. You can also capture a single browser tab, or just your camera. A circular webcam bubble can be composited into a screen recording, and moved between corners while you record. Does it slow down the pages I browse? No. There is no content script running on the pages you visit. Code is injected into a page only at the moment you ask for a capture of that page, and Chrome revokes that access as soon as you navigate away. On every other page, the extension is doing nothing at all. What happens to my captures if I uninstall the extension? They are deleted along with the extension's storage, because that storage is the only place they exist. Download anything you want to keep before uninstalling. The library offers a bulk download for exactly this. Is there a Firefox, Edge or Safari version? Not yet. Screen Awesome is built for Chrome's Manifest V3 and uses Chrome-specific capture APIs. It should install on Chromium-based browsers such as Edge, Brave and Opera, though that is not what it is tested against. How do I report a bug or request a feature? Email nitinbhaiviras@gmail.com with what you were doing and what happened. Bug reports that mention the recording target you chose, whether the microphone or camera was on, and any notification text you saw are the fastest ones to fix. Start recording in about ten seconds Install it, click the toolbar icon, choose a screen or a tab. Nothing to configure, nothing to sign up for, nothing leaving your machine. products.name: Finyuus
products.tagline: A code-first language for durable, governed AI workflows
products.description: Finyuus is a code-first platform for building, running, and governing AI workflows. It introduces a small indentation-based DSL for composing agents, tools, guards, human approvals, and nested workflows — then runs them on Temporal with retries, cancellation, and replayability. Unlike visual builders, workflows are stored as text for Git-based review and diffs. Unlike prompt chains, every run is durable, versioned, observable via Langfuse, and governable through guards and human approvals.

Save your favorite spots, add photos and tips, and it becomes a visual guide you can share with one link. No more scattered screenshots or 47 tab Google Docs. Make it yours with custom fonts, colors, stickers, backgrounds, and themes. Or drop a screenshot in and let AI build it for you. Real recs from real people. Works for Tokyo or your favorite spots around the corner.

products.what_it_sells: Free, open-source voice dictation and AI assistant, offline
products.problem_solved: SpeakoFlow puts your voice over your whole desktop. Speak, and your words land in any app — email, editor, chat, terminal. Say "Hey Flow" and it writes the whole reply from what's on your screen. Ask the assistant about what you're looking at and hear the answer back. It also cleans up your dictation, translates as you speak, and learns how you work. Everything can run on your machine — speech-to-text always does. Free, open source, MIT. Windows, macOS, Linux.

products.what_it_sells: A code-first language for durable, governed AI workflows
products.problem_solved: Finyuus is a code-first platform for building, running, and governing AI workflows. It introduces a small indentation-based DSL for composing agents, tools, guards, human approvals, and nested workflows — then runs them on Temporal with retries, cancellation, and replayability. Unlike visual builders, workflows are stored as text for Git-based review and diffs. Unlike prompt chains, every run is durable, versioned, observable via Langfuse, and governable through guards and human approvals.
